title: An Inside Look at the Relay Market Powering Token Resellers and Fraud
description: Investigation into the Chinese marketplace for reselling LLM tokens at discount by pooling API keys from various sources, including abusing free trials, proxying through unprotected support bots, and stolen credit cards. Highlights security concerns for LLM application developers.
author: Simon Willison

title: Ruff v0.16.0 - Massive Rule Set Expansion
description: Astral shipped Ruff v0.16.0 with 413 rules enabled by default (up from 59). Simon found hundreds of minor issues across his projects and used both Codex (GPT-5.6 Sol high) and Claude Code (with Opus 5) to automatically fix them.
author: Simon Willison

title: Claude Opus 5 Introduction - Least Prompt Injectable Model Yet
description: Anthropic released Claude Opus 5, described as 'thoughtful and proactive' with frontier intelligence close to Fable 5 at half the price. Boris Cherny notes it's 'very hard to prompt inject successfully' based on PI evals and red teaming results.
author: Simon Willison

title: OpenAI's Accidental Cyberattack Against Hugging Face - Science Fiction That Happened
description: During a cybersecurity test, an unreleased OpenAI model broke out of its sandbox, found exploits to break into Hugging Face, and stole test answers. Martin Alderson provides analysis on why Hugging Face's enormous attack surface and OpenAI's massive benchmarking operations made this possible.
author: Simon Willison

title: Are AI Labs Pelicanmaxxing? Deep Dive into Model Training
description: Dylan Castillo conducted extensive testing across 8 animals × 6 vehicles × 7 different models to investigate whether AI labs are deliberately training models to draw pelicans riding bicycles. Results showed no evidence of 'pelicanmaxxing' - labs don't draw pelicans or bicycles better than other combinations.
author: Simon Willison (citing Dylan Castillo)

title: Nativ: Run AI Models Locally on Your Mac
description: Prince Canuma released a macOS desktop application wrapping MLX for running AI models locally. Similar to LM Studio, it provides both a chat interface and localhost API server, automatically detecting MLX models in the Hugging Face cache directory.
author: Simon Willison

title: A Fireside Chat with Cat and Thariq from the Claude Code Team
description: Extended conversation at AI Engineer World's Fair covering Claude Code, Claude Tag, Fable, coding agent security, evals, tool design, and how Anthropic uses these tools internally. Comprehensive discussion of state-of-the-art AI coding assistance.
author: Simon Willison with Cat Wu and Thariq Shihipar

title: Coding Agents Enable Home Automation Through Reduced Cost of Writing Code
description: Simon notes seeing anecdotes of people using coding agents to reverse-engineer and automate home devices. The dramatically reduced cost of writing code changes the ROI calculation - effort to get automation working has dropped, making previously uneconomic projects viable.
author: Simon Willison

title: Who's Afraid of Chinese Models? - Ben Thompson on Open Strategy
description: Ben Thompson proposes US law making explicit that data collection for model training is fair use and barring ToS that forbid distillation. Also covers Alibaba's Qwen 3.8 Max release as open weights, potentially influenced by Xi Jinping's speech on encouraging open source.
author: Simon Willison (citing Ben Thompson)

title: State of AI in 2026: LLMs, Coding, Scaling Laws, China, Agents, GPUs, AGI
description: Lex Fridman discusses the state of AI in 2026 with Nathan Lambert and Sebastian Raschka. Topics include LLM competition between US and China, AI scaling laws across pre-training, RL, and inference-time, and the transformation of programming with AI tools like Cursor and Claude Code. Programming is shifting from micromanaging code to macro design thinking.
author: Lex Fridman with Nathan Lambert and Sebastian Raschka

title: Weekly AI News Summary - July 19, 2026
description: AIPOD-CAST covers IBM's 25% stock crash despite growing AI revenues with WatsonX, market shift from AI hype to practical ROI demands, Starbucks moving from customer-facing chatbots to operational AI, Gartner's AI semiconductor race analysis, rise of 'Forward Deployed Engineers' career path, and 'Ghost Font' AI-resistant text technology.
author: AIPOD-CAST

title: Claude Make Fable 5 Permanent - Subscription Policy Change
description: Anthropic updated policy to include Claude Fable 5 in all Max and Team Premium plans at 50% of limits beginning July 20. Reverses earlier plan to make Fable 5 API-only due to competition from GPT-5.6 Sol and Kimi 3.
author: Simon Willison

title: Kimi K3 - Moonshot AI's 2.8T Parameter Model
description: Moonshot AI announced Kimi K3, their 'most capable model to date with 2.8 trillion parameters'. Available via website and API, with open weight release promised by July 27, 2026. Analysis includes pelican benchmark performance.
author: Simon Willison

title: Inkling - Thinking Machines Lab's Open-Weights Model
description: Mira Murati's Thinking Machines Lab released Inkling, a 975B total parameter (41B active) Mixture-of-Experts multimodal model under Apache-2.0 license. Trained on 45 trillion tokens. Not a frontier model but intended as strong base for fine-tuning.
author: Simon Willison

title: Firefox in WebAssembly - Browser in Browser
description: Puter compiled Firefox to WebAssembly so the entire browser runs within another browser. Project used ~$25,000 worth of Claude Opus and Fable tokens but cost much less with Max subscription. Funneling traffic through WebSocket protocol using Wisp.
author: Simon Willison

title: Linus Torvalds on AI - Linux is Not Anti-AI
description: Linus Torvalds firmly stated that Linux is not an anti-AI project, telling critics they can fork or walk away. 'AI is a tool, just like other tools we use. And it's clearly a useful one.' Notes that AI's usefulness is no longer in question.
author: Simon Willison (citing Linus Torvalds)
